explain.say: People cool down by sweating all over, but dogs have sweat glands that cool them mainly in their paw pads, and a fur coat that holds heat in. So they need another way to lose heat.

faq.a: Only a little. Dogs have sweat glands that cool mainly in their paw pads, which is why they may leave damp footprints on a hot day. Most of their cooling comes from panting.
asks: Why don't dogs sweat like people?

faq.q: How does panting cool a dog?
faq.a: Turning water into vapour needs heat, which is taken from the dog's tongue, mouth and nose. Blood flowing through those wet surfaces cools down and carries the coolness back into the body.
asks: Why do dogs stick their tongues out?

faq.q: How fast does a dog pant?
faq.a: A hot dog can pant around 300 to 400 times a minute. The quick, shallow breaths mostly move air in and out of the nose, mouth and windpipe, where cooling happens.
asks: How many breaths does a panting dog take?

faq.q: Why is it dangerous to leave a dog in a hot car?
faq.a: A parked car heats up fast, and the air inside gets hot and humid, so panting stops working well. A dog can get heatstroke within minutes, which can kill it.
asks: How quickly can a dog overheat?

faq.q: Why do flat-faced dogs struggle in the heat?
faq.a: Breeds with short muzzles, like pugs and bulldogs, have smaller noses and airways, so less wet surface for cooling and harder breathing. They overheat more easily.
asks: Are pugs bad in hot weather?

facts: Dogs lose heat mainly by panting, which evaporates water from the tongue, mouth and upper airways.
Dogs' cooling sweat glands are found mainly in their paw pads.
